concepts.title: HTTP Request Lifecycle
concepts.description: How an HTTP request travels from the client through network and OS boundaries to a backend service.

outcomes.competency: Trace an HTTP request from client to server across network and runtime boundaries.
outcomes.evidence: Draw POST /transfers and classify six failures by boundary.

assessment.task: Trace POST /transfers across a client, transport boundary, server and controller. Explain what fails at each boundary.

criteria.check: Identify the request sequence across client, DNS/TCP transport and HTTP application.
criteria.passWhen: The trace names the responsible boundary for each hop and does not treat a network failure as an HTTP status.

criteria.check: Explain what the controller validates and which HTTP response it returns.
criteria.passWhen: Spring MVC code and a controller-slice test show request validation, HTTP response mapping and service delegation; the standalone JDK fixture alone does not test Spring wiring.

criteria.check: Reproduce a localhost-only service unreachable from another namespace.
criteria.passWhen: Actual peer-netns curl and host ss/ip observations identify the loopback-only binding; a same-namespace 127.0.0.2 fixture is not sufficient.

outcomes.competency: Diagnose failed requests where the server process is running but the endpoint is unavailable.
outcomes.evidence: Prove a remote-binding failure, then describe correct readiness behavior under DB outage.

assessment.task: Investigate a running service that cannot receive remote traffic, then diagnose an unhealthy dependency.

criteria.check: Distinguish interface-binding failure from a process crash.
criteria.passWhen: Listener address, host/peer route state and curl evidence from a separate namespace distinguish binding failure from process crash, then verify the scoped rebind.

criteria.check: Explain how a database outage changes readiness without changing liveness.
criteria.passWhen: A real Spring Boot plus Kubernetes outage test shows /ready failing and regular Service endpoints excluded while liveness remains healthy; the Node status fixture alone cannot prove traffic routing.

concepts.title: TCP Connection Lifecycle
concepts.description: Connection establishment, acknowledgement, retransmission, and closure before HTTP application handling.

outcomes.competency: Explain TCP connection establishment and retransmission.
outcomes.evidence: Capture and explain a TCP handshake and one retransmission.

assessment.task: Capture one TCP session and explain how connection setup or retransmission affects HTTP reachability.

criteria.check: Identify SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK from a connection trace.
criteria.passWhen: An actual TCP packet trace shows SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK with correct endpoints and sequence.

criteria.check: Distinguish a transport retransmission/timeout from a completed HTTP error response.
criteria.passWhen: A real trace identifies transport retransmission or timeout before any HTTP response; the learner does not invent an HTTP status.

concepts.title: Server Address & Binding
concepts.description: Loopback addresses, interfaces, bind addresses, and access across network namespaces.

outcomes.competency: Explain loopback vs remotely reachable listening addresses.
outcomes.evidence: Reproduce a localhost-only endpoint failure from another network namespace.

assessment.task: Demonstrate loopback-only versus peer-accessible listening across a real Linux network namespace with veth, routes and access policy. A local alias probe alone is insufficient.

criteria.check: Report address, interface and port for each listener configuration.
criteria.passWhen: Observed ss, ip addr and bound interface/port distinguish loopback-only from veth-specific and wildcard IPv4 listeners.

criteria.check: Test connectivity from a separate network namespace.
criteria.passWhen: Command output from ip netns exec curl in a genuine peer namespace and host ss shows failed and recovered connectivity; same-namespace aliases do not count.

concepts.title: HTTP Controller Contract
concepts.description: Endpoint routing, HTTP methods, status codes, and the application boundary.

outcomes.competency: Define an HTTP controller contract with correct status codes.
outcomes.evidence: Implement transfer POST/GET responses without business logic in the controller.

assessment.task: Specify and implement a small HTTP controller contract without moving business rules into the controller.

criteria.check: Define POST/GET routes and their success/error response mapping.
criteria.passWhen: A real Spring MVC MockMvc/controller test proves POST 201/Location, GET 200/404 and input validation 400; the JDK fixture tests only HTTP status design.

criteria.check: Explain which work belongs in the controller versus the service layer.
criteria.passWhen: A code example or call flow locates validation and HTTP mapping at the edge while business logic remains separate.

concepts.title: Service Readiness
concepts.description: Service readiness, liveness, dependencies, and the conditions for accepting traffic.

assessment.task: Define and demonstrate distinct liveness and readiness behavior during service startup.

criteria.check: State what liveness reports while the process is running.
criteria.passWhen: A Spring Boot probe or availability-state test demonstrates liveness after process startup without coupling it to an unrelated downstream health failure; the HTTP listener may be unavailable before startup.

criteria.check: State when the service should be admitted to receive traffic.
criteria.passWhen: The Spring Boot readiness group remains unready until essential initialization is complete; health-state observations are distinguished from the separate Node simulation.

outcomes.competency: Diagnose service availability during slow startup and DB outages.
outcomes.evidence: Simulate a dependency failure; verify readiness rejects traffic without triggering restart loops.

assessment.task: Run a controlled downstream outage and explain safe readiness and recovery decisions.

criteria.check: Demonstrate readiness response during and after a database outage.
criteria.passWhen: A real Spring Boot DB fault injection plus Kubernetes Service/EndpointSlice observation verifies that readiness blocks regular traffic during outage and recovers afterwards.

criteria.check: Explain why liveness must not repeatedly restart a healthy process during a downstream outage.
criteria.passWhen: A real cluster observation shows the shared DB outage alone does not cause liveness-driven container restarts; a local 200/503 fixture cannot establish restart counts.

concepts.title: Java Build & Spring Boot Startup
concepts.description: Java 21 compiler/runtime, Maven scope and packaging are separate contracts from whether a Spring Boot HTTP service starts and responds.

outcomes.competency: Reproduce Java 21 CLI builds and distinguish toolchain, compile, packaging and Spring service-start failures.
outcomes.evidence: Demonstrate a Java 21 Maven clean build and executable artifact, then start a Spring Boot /ping endpoint from the CLI.

assessment.task: Diagnose a broken Java 21 CLI build, then separately verify Spring Boot can start and serve /ping without an IDE.

criteria.check: Identify build-time versus runtime failure and correct the JDK/dependency scope.
criteria.passWhen: A real Java 21 command transcript shows JDK versions, Maven clean verify and java -jar execution after the repair; the standalone compiler fixture is insufficient.

criteria.check: Start a real Java 21 Spring Boot application and confirm the request path.
criteria.passWhen: A Spring Boot process started via Maven or its executable JAR responds HTTP 200 to /ping and the CLI test/package steps succeed; no simulated response is accepted.

concepts.title: Relational Schema & SQL
concepts.description: SQL relations, primary/foreign keys, ownership and repeatable schema initialization turn transfer/account data requirements into explicit PostgreSQL constraints.

outcomes.competency: Create a repeatable PostgreSQL sandbox for accounts and transfers and validate relational ownership and key constraints.
outcomes.evidence: Run init.sql and inspection queries against a disposable PostgreSQL database; verify declared relationships using real database results.

assessment.task: Define account/transfer tables and test the specified customer-account ownership model against an actual PostgreSQL instance, not a diagram alone.

criteria.check: Initialize accounts/transfers schema and explain relational keys using SQL.
criteria.passWhen: An actual disposable PostgreSQL session runs the repeatable init.sql in a fresh database and six inspection queries return the expected schema and sample rows.

criteria.check: Model customer/account/transfer cardinality, including invalid ownership under the chosen policy.
criteria.passWhen: A PostgreSQL-backed DDL/fixture demonstrates the chosen customer ownership and FK/PK constraints, rejecting invalid ownership cases per the explicitly documented policy.

concepts.title: API Contract Testing
concepts.description: A documented transfer HTTP contract is checked at the API boundary: response statuses, request/response shapes and backward-compatible schema evolution.

outcomes.competency: Test the externally observable transfer API contract and detect incompatible changes without conflating tests with implementation details.
outcomes.evidence: Execute real API contract cases and a deliberate breaking-schema mutation; distinguish success, client and server response families.

assessment.task: Build a small contract matrix from the transfer OpenAPI document; run tests against a real HTTP implementation and prove the suite catches contract drift.

criteria.check: Specify OpenAPI schemas and stable transfer response/error behavior.
criteria.passWhen: A published OpenAPI document, runnable HTTP contract tests and a documented backward-compatible change agree on request/response shapes, repeat keys and error semantics.

criteria.check: Run happy-path and negative HTTP boundary cases for transfers/accounts.
criteria.passWhen: API tests execute real endpoints and assert each contractually applicable status, content type, headers and stable error body; unsupported responses are not invented.

criteria.check: Detect a removed required field or changed field type while accepting an optional extension.
criteria.passWhen: A spec-driven test suite fails for an intentionally breaking required-field/type mutation and passes for a compatible optional-field addition.

concepts.title: Transfer API Design Contract
concepts.description: System design defines HTTP resources, status semantics and client compatibility; the Spring controller implements that externally observable contract.

outcomes.competency: Specify transfer/account API resources and check that a Spring HTTP controller preserves the designed request and response contracts.
outcomes.evidence: Produce a concrete transfer API specification and independently verify selected POST/GET response mappings against a real Spring controller.

assessment.task: Define the transfer API contract, explain client-visible error semantics and compare a Spring controller's behavior against the spec.

criteria.check: Specify POST /transfers, GET /transfers/{id} and GET /accounts/{id} with payloads and failure cases.
criteria.passWhen: A written contract supplies example request/response bodies, reasons for 201/400/401/403/409/500 choices and one backward-compatible evolution; it does not claim implementation proof.

criteria.check: Compare controller POST/GET status and validation behavior against the API design.
criteria.passWhen: An actual Spring MVC test proves agreed POST 201/Location, GET 200/404 and invalid input 400 without moving business rules into controller code; the JDK fixture alone is insufficient.

relations.rationale: Connection behavior explains failures before application handling.
The listening address determines whether requests can reach a process.
A controller interprets the request after transport delivery.
Operational health determines whether a service should receive traffic.
A Spring MVC controller runs within a Java application; build and runtime failures must be distinguished from HTTP routing.
The Spring controller implements the interface contract defined for client-visible transfer resources and errors.
Contract tests check whether an implementation preserves the documented response schema and status semantics.
Transfer/account resource boundaries relate to relational data modeling, but an API resource is not automatically a database table.
Maven test and Java toolchain behavior affect reproducibility of Java-based API contract suites.
